title: Post-write invalidation closes one stale-fill window
dek: Post-write deletion removes cache fills that finish during the write, but an older in-flight snapshot can refill the cache afterward.
footer: The model uses one shared Map, without a generation check for readers.

sections.title: Early deletion left a window for stale fills
sections.content: The old update deleted the cached entry before awaiting the database write. A cache miss could read and cache the old stored value during that wait.

sections.title: Delete only after the write fulfills
sections.content: The changed update deletes after the write succeeds. It removes an old cache fill that completed during the write. A failed write leaves an existing cached entry in place. In the sequential example, the next read sees the new stored value.

sections.title: An older snapshot can arrive after deletion
sections.content: The author says concurrent stale reads are removed, but read is unchanged. The modeled reader captures the old database value, waits through the update and deletion, then caches that old value. A subsequent read returns the stale entry. The change supplies no generation check or in-flight reader synchronization.

sections.title: Close one cache-fill window
sections.content: Moving deletion after a successful write closes the window for fills that finish during that write. It does not prevent stale results from overlapping readers or late cache fills.
